app.title: PlateMaster - Dashboard for Plate Analysis
app.summary: A person loads one or more plate-reader workbooks, from a folder, by upload or as a ZIP. They choose the worksheet, header row and expected plate size, and each file's time is taken from its filename. They preview each parsed plate. Then they choose rows and columns and decide how wells are pooled: by column, by row, or by named groups typed into a plate-map grid or loaded from a CSV. They also choose an aggregation and an optional outlier rule. After pressing Run they get one aggregated table across all files, with descriptive statistics, a Welch t-test between two chosen groups, an optional pairwise p-value matrix, a log of removed outliers and a cross-file chart with error bars. Finally they export an Excel report that records provenance, along with the plate map and a reloadable settings file.

task.text: Pool replicate wells from multi-well plate readouts across time-point files into group values, test differences between groups, and export a reproducible report.

data.text: Plate-reader measurement matrices, one spreadsheet per time point, with lettered rows and numbered columns of numeric readings, plus an optional map that assigns wells to named groups.
data.item: a well on a multi-well plate, read once in each time-point file

stage.text: analyzing plate-reader readouts after the run, before writing up

mechanism.text: Sidebar controls set the source, selection, pooling layout, aggregation and outlier rule, and Run recomputes everything below them. In the main area, the colour-graded preview, plate-map grid, aggregated table, statistics selectors, outlier log and chart all read from the same pooled values. Settings and plate maps can be saved and reloaded so the analysis can be replayed.

workflow.name: pool replicates into groups and test differences between groups

steps.here: Load a server folder, uploaded workbooks or a ZIP. Import options set the worksheet, the header row, an expected plate size (6 to 1536 wells) and an opt-in for custom labels. Each file is validated, and its time is the last number in its filename.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: A Preview file selector shows each parsed plate as a colour-graded table, along with import warnings and the plate dimensions.

Pick rows and columns and an aggregation layout: by original columns, by original rows, or by plate groups. In plate-group mode, wells are labelled with group names in an editable plate grid, or a row_id,column,group CSV is applied, and the map can be downloaded.

Choose Mean, Median, Min, Max, Std or Sum, plus an optional IQR, Z-score or MAD filter with a strictness slider, then press Run. Removed wells are logged by file, row and column, with removal percentages.

Pick a time and a column to get n, mean, SD, SEM, a Student-t 95% CI and a one-sample test. Pick Group A and Group B (time and column) for a Welch t-test. Optionally, choose 2 to 20 time and metric groups for a lower-triangle matrix of unadjusted pairwise p-values.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: The cross-file chart plots the pooled values against time or by column, as line, scatter, bar, box or violin. Error bars can show SD, SEM, 95% CI, IQR/2 or MAD; SEM and CI are offered only with Mean.

Export report.xlsx writes the aggregated, statistics, t-test, outlier and plot sheets, plus the settings, plate groups, input checksums and software versions. Download settings.json saves a replayable configuration.

distinctive: Each file's time point comes from the last number in its filename, so a folder of plate exports becomes a time course.
Plates are validated against a chosen plate format with lettered rows and numbered columns. Non-standard labels are rejected unless the person explicitly allows them.
Wells can be pooled by column, by row, or by named groups from a plate map that can be typed into a grid or round-tripped as CSV.
Statistics follow fixed rules: Welch tests, Student-t intervals, and pairwise p-values flagged as unadjusted with a warning that technical wells are not independent replicates.
Settings JSON and the report record file checksums and software versions. Reloading settings warns when the inputs or environment differ from the original run.
